# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds, about $199 (list $299)**
Runner's World's top pick, with clear sound, a comfortable clip design, and little sound leakage. Wired likes the physical buttons, which are easier to use mid-run. Battery is about 7 hours (19.5 with the case) and water resistance is only IPX4, so they're not ideal for heavy rain. Runner's World also says Bose has a new pair coming soon, so you may want to wait.
[Runner's World review and buy links](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) · [Wired's guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, $180 list, about $125 at Best Buy and REI**
This is the pick if hearing traffic is your top priority. It has 12 hours of battery, an IP55 rating, and physical buttons. Wired says it has bigger bass than the older model but less clarity, and the neckband can interfere with long hair and winter hats.
[Wired review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/) · [RTINGS comparison with the Bose](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

**Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2, $200**
Wired's overall pick. It has 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating, so it handles rain and sweat easily. The clip-on design leaves the top of your ear free for hats and sunglasses.
[Wired's guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best value: Soundcore AeroFit 2, about $80**
SoundGuys calls it the best budget pick. It has an IP55 rating, 10 hours per charge (42 with the case), and a hook design. SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 on Amazon. Dealectric lists it at $129.99 at Soundcore's own store, or about $104 with code AFSC20. Check Amazon first, since it's cheaper unless prices have changed.
[Buy at Soundcore (affiliate link)](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2) · [SoundGuys picks](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Cheapest way to try the style: JLab Flex Open, about $40–50**
Runner's World calls it the lowest-risk way to see if clip-ons work for you. Sound is less detailed, and it has touch controls only. The Wired alternative is the Soundpeats PearlClip Pro at about $50.
[Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Also worth a look: Nothing Ear (Open), about $99 on Amazon**
SoundGuys rates it best overall and best for running, with strong bass for an open design and an IP54 rating.
[SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

## Quick advice
- **Most aware of traffic:** bone conduction (OpenRun Pro 2).
- **Best sound:** Bose.
- **Rain or marathon-length runs:** OpenDots 2.
- **Tight budget:** AeroFit 2 or JLab Flex Open.

Open-ear styles won't block traffic noise, but Runner's World notes they don't guarantee safety, so keep the volume moderate.
